# Genetic Counselor Leaders {-}

## How can GARDE help the genetic counseling team? {-}

<div style="float:left; width:40%; margin:0 30px 20px 0;">
  <img src="resources/images/GARDE-process.png" style="width:100%; display:block;">

  <p style="font-size:0.8em; line-height:1.4; margin:10px 0 0 0;">
    <strong>Figure 1.</strong> GARDE process.
  </p>
</div>

<p style="line-height:1.75; margin-top:0;">
  The demand for clinicians with genetics expertise is increasing and the supply of genetic counselors isn’t keeping pace with the growing demand.
</p>

<div style="float:right; width:34%; border-top:4px solid black; border-bottom:4px solid black; padding:15px 0; margin:10px 0 20px 30px;">
  <p style="margin:0 0 15px 0;">
    <em>“With GARDE and the chatbot, we were able to customize patient interactions so that our patients still knew a human was involved in their care.”</em>
  </p>
  <p style="margin:0;">
    — Genetic Counselor leader from an implementation site
  </p>
</div>

<p style="line-height:1.75;">
  GARDE facilitates the population-based identification of high-risk patients based on data already available in the EHR. Patient outreach and education occur through a <a href="https://garde.utah.edu/garde-chat.html">customizable chatbot</a>. Under a genetic counselor’s supervision, a genetic counseling assistant enters genetic test orders for patients who choose to pursue genetic testing. GARDE allows genetic counselors to focus on patients with more complex needs.
</p>

<div style="clear:both;"></div>

## How can GARDE help my patients? {-}

We anticipate that GARDE with a chatbot will allow genetic counselors to prioritize patient psychosocial needs over education and information-gathering tasks while maintaining patient satisfaction with the care they receive tasks (see PMID: [33191601](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33191601/)) while maintaining patient satisfaction with the care they receive (see PMCID: [PMC8663668](https://www.jmir.org/2021/11/e29447/) and [PMC11385050](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2823183)).

## I’m concerned about GARDE having access to confidential patient information. {-}

So are we. That’s why GARDE is designed to run on your organization’s servers. It doesn’t increase the risk of a security breach and your patients’ confidential information remains secure. 

## What kind of genetic tests are appropriate for patients identified by GARDE? {-}
A patient’s genetic test is selected by a genetic counselor based on the same criteria the counselor uses to select the most appropriate genetic test for any patient. In [previous research](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2823183), a 34-36 gene pan-cancer panel was typically ordered on patients identified by GARDE population health management algorithms. 

## How do patients identified by GARDE pay for genetic testing? {-}

If a GARDE population health management algorithm is used to identify patients who may be at elevated risk to harbor a pathogenic variant in a hereditary cancer gene, patients identified by GARDE pay for genetic testing the same way as patients who are identified by a clinician. 

## Have other cancer genetic counseling teams used GARDE? {-}

NCI supported a successful trial of GARDE at University of Utah Health and New York University Langone Health. With National Cancer Institute support, GARDE is being implemented at Medical University of South Carolina and Weil Cornell Medicine. The [GARDE study team](mailto:GARDE@hci.utah.edu) is happy to speak with you if you have questions that aren’t addressed here. Research publications demonstrating GARDE’s effectiveness can be found [here](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=CA204800&sort=date).
